title: 400 million Chinese cannot speak Mandarin
synopsis: According to government statistics, 400 million people in China do not speak Mandarin. In this lesson we take a closer look at this phenomenon in today’s China.

fullText.simplified:
中国4亿人不会说普通话

    知道吗！中国仍有约4亿人不会说普通话。
    据教育部统计，现在中国有70%的人口会说普通话，95%以上的识字人口使用规范汉字。也就是说，全国仍然有30%的人口，相当于4亿人不能用普通话进行交流。
    的确是这样的。有些城市，甚至以不会用方言为耻。一些地方的中小学校，课下的交流普遍使用地方方言，很少使用普通话交流。老师们也是课上使用普通话，平时一般用方言与学生交流。
    方言当然重要，但是只会说方言，就无法和别的地方的人交流了。比如一些不是本地的家长会非常担心孩子在普遍使用方言的学校里上学，难以融入到同学当中去。我们处在信息社会，随着人们活动范围和方式的不断扩大，跨地域交流越来越多，会说普通话真的越来越重要了。
fullText.traditional:
中國4億人不會說普通話

    知道嗎！中國仍有約4億人不會說普通話。
    據教育部統計，現在中國有70%的人口會說普通話，95%以上的識字人口使用規範漢字。也就是說，全國仍然有30%的人口，相當於4億人不能用普通話進行交流。
    的確是這樣的。有些城市，甚至以不會用方言為恥。一些地方的中小學校，課下的交流普遍使用地方方言，很少使用普通話交流。老師們也是課上使用普通話，平時一般用方言與學生交流。
    方言當然重要，但是只會說方言，就無法和別的地方的人交流了。比如一些不是本地的家長會非常擔心孩子在普遍使用方言的學校裡上學，難以融入到同學當中去。我們處在信息社會，隨著人們活動範圍和方式的不斷擴大，跨地域交流越來越多，會說普通話真的越來越重要了。

raw.synopsis: According to government statistics, 400 million people in China do not speak Mandarin. In this lesson we take a closer look at this phenomenon in today’s China.
sentence_translations: Did you know? There are still about 400 million people in China who cannot speak Mandarin.
According to statistics by the Ministry of Education, at present 70% of China's population can speak Mandarin, ..
.. and over 95% of the literate population uses standard Chinese characters.
That is, the remaining 30% of the national population, corresponding to 400 million people, can not use Mandarin to communicate.
In some cities, not being able to speak the local dialect is even seen as something shameful.
In primary and middle school in some regions, interaction outside class is usually done using the local dialect, and seldom using Mandarin.
Even the teachers use Mandarin during class, but apart from that mostly communicate with the students using dialect.
Dialect is certainly important, but if you can only speak dialect you have no way of interacting with people from other regions.
For example, some parents coming from other regions to schools which mainly use dialect worry whether their children will have a hard time integrating with their classmates.
We live in an information society, and as people's range of movement expands, inter-regional communication is becoming more common, ..
.. and the ability to speak Mandarin really is becoming more and more important.
